html:
A French officer who was governor of Senegal from 1854 to 1865 and began the conquest of the interior from Saint-Louis.

He built forts up the Senegal River, held off Umar Tall at the siege of Medine in 1857, and annexed Walo and other Wolof lands. In 1857 he created the Senegalese Tirailleurs, the African soldiers who later conquered much of the continent for France. He founded a school for chiefs' sons and pushed the groundnut trade. His methods, of forts, African troops and alliances with chiefs, set the pattern for the French empire in Africa. His statue in Saint-Louis is now contested.
sum: A French officer who was governor of Senegal from 1854 to 1865 and began the conquest of the interior from Saint-Louis.
